title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 410
paragraphs: When the Egyptians turned and fled from the battle, they fled in disorder; and as they were shut up in Memphis, Cambyses sent a ship from Mytilene up the river carrying a Persian herald to summon the Egyptians to terms of surrender. But when they saw the ship entering Memphis, they poured forth from the fortress in a body, destroyed the ship, and tore the men in it limb from limb, and carried their remains into the fortress. After this, the Egyptians, being besieged, surrendered in due course. The Libyans who dwell on the borders of Egypt, struck with terror by what had happened to Egypt, surrendered themselves without resistance, both imposing a tribute on themselves and sending presents. Likewise the people of Kyrene and Barca, equally terrified with the Libyans, acted in a similar way. Cambyses accepted the gifts from the Libyans graciously, but as for the gifts from the Kyrenians, finding fault with them — I suppose because they were too small in amount (for the Kyrenians in fact sent five hundred pounds of silver) — he took the silver by handfuls and scattered it with his own hand among his soldiers.
